sealed.statement: Runtime replica lifecycle completion hands desired state to one production-wired retained projection owner without waiting on services-table writes; that owner composes ServicesOwner and the existing owner-key reconcile queue to serialize and coalesce the latest state per replica and retry typed failures, and three consecutive fresh MovieLens runs report priority metric 0.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Compose the existing ServicesOwner mutation boundary and OwnerKeyReconcileQueue retry/serialization primitive. Do not add feature-local retry timers, retry maps, raw SQL, a second services-table writer, direct cache repair, or a lifecycle-state authority outside ServiceRuntimeLifecycle.

ServiceRuntimeLifecycle must return from projection submission without awaiting the routed control-plane write or its retry budget. The projection owner must retain accepted work per service replica independently of the source replica-operation deadline and expose accepted, applied, retrying, permanent-failure, and shutdown state through inspectable events or diagnostics.

At most one services projection executes per service replica at a time. A newer desired transition received while an older transition is in flight or retained for retry replaces the pending context; CREATED must never overwrite ACTIVE or FAILED, ACTIVE must never resurrect STOPPED, and rapid transitions for different service replicas may progress independently.

Preserve TEST-0001 and ARCH-0009: the first non-STOPPED projection creates the canonical identity once only after primary-key UPDATE proves the row absent; later transitions UPDATE by service_id; STOPPED DELETEs; FAILED remains visible. Never use UPSERT, INSERT OR REPLACE, full-row replacement, or observer/cache writes.

Retry only failures classified by the canonical control-plane error classifier and honor its retryAfterMs. A non-retryable failure must be surfaced once and dropped without a hot loop; a retryable failure remains retained until a newer state supersedes it, it applies, or owner shutdown clears it.

SQL/runtime shutdown must stop the projection reconcile queue and clear its timers and retained in-memory work. Do not invent disk durability: after process restart, the existing runtime placement/re-drive path remains responsible for resubmitting desired lifecycle state.

Do not change replica-operation deadlines, transition budgets, gateway timeouts, retry constants, rebalancer cadence or concurrency, MovieLens workload, preload size, schema stability or ordinary-release timing, stall/convergence budgets, affinity scoring, live runner ordering, or exact-result predicates.

Before live validation, prove through the production ServiceRuntimeLifecycle-to-SQL projection composition that lifecycle completion is not held by a blocked CREATED write, a later ACTIVE state applies after the retryable CREATED failure without stale replay, STOPPED cannot be resurrected by an older in-flight state, permanent failures do not retry, and the test is red when the retained projection owner wiring is reverted.
Run npm run model:contracts before the live gate and retain architecture/contracts/core-system-logic.md as the model-rung reference.

Use the unchanged ordered live runner: five formation probes must pass before three measuring MovieLens repetitions; stop on the first red, preserve immutable stopped-state evidence, and do not make an unchanged rerun.
